action_items: Address tech-debt items flagged in critical_code_review_comments (no functional bugs found in iter5).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1297 lines (was 1152 in iter4, 700-line threshold flagged since iter3). Bulk-import endpoints add another ~110 lines to the monolith. Strongly recommend splitting into routers: routers/auth.py, routers/teams.py, routers/players.py, routers/matches.py, routers/fixtures.py, routers/inventory.py, routers/bookings.py, routers/uploads.py, routers/imports.py.

_parse_uploaded() does no validation of header set against the expected template - a CSV with completely wrong columns silently produces rows where every required value is empty, returning N 'Falta el nombre del equipo' errors. Better UX: detect 'no expected headers found' upfront and return a single clear error 'Encabezados inválidos. Use la plantilla descargable.'

import_teams / import_players use insert_many AFTER full validation pass but before any DB-level uniqueness check. Two CSVs with the same team name (case difference) will create duplicate teams. Consider adding a pre-insert duplicate check against db.teams or a unique compound index on (name, category).

TeamOut and PlayerOut Pydantic models do not include the 'status' field, so it is silently stripped from every public/admin GET response. The admin /aprobaciones page uses the status query filter (q.status=...) which works at the DB level, but consumers cannot read status off a single team object - they must round-trip via the filter. Add status: Optional[str] = 'aprobado' to TeamOut/PlayerOut so it round-trips properly.

import_teams accepts raw query string preview=true/false. FastAPI's bool casting is lenient but a value like ?preview=foo is treated as truthy (preview=True, no save). Recommend: preview: bool = Query(False) and document explicitly, or switch to ?save=true semantics.
import_players' team_name lookup is built from db.teams.find({}) capped at 2000 docs. For a tournament with >2000 historical teams this will silently miss matches. Either remove the cap or paginate.

5MB cap is enforced AFTER awaiting file.read() (full body buffered into RAM). A malicious 500MB upload still consumes memory before the 400. Use UploadFile streaming with a chunk-counting wrapper or rely on a server-level limit (e.g., starlette's max_request_size).

openpyxl load_workbook(data_only=True) is correct but xlrd==1.2.0 is in requirements.txt yet never imported - it predates xlsx support and is dead weight. Remove unless .xls (legacy) is a planned input format.

import_teams/players default 'status': 'aprobado' bypasses the approval workflow added in iter4. Document this clearly in admin UX (the AdminBulkUpload.jsx already calls the page 'Carga masiva' but should display a hint like 'Los registros importados quedan auto-aprobados').

AdminBulkUpload.jsx: the 'Confirmar e importar' button is only shown when result && !result.saved && result.ok > 0. After a successful save, if the user picks a NEW file the previous result lingers and the new preview workflow is unclear. Consider clearing result when file changes (already cleared on file pick - good) and after successful save reset file too.

AdminBulkUpload uses formatApiError(err.response?.data?.detail) but the toast.error('...') falls back to 'Error al importar' if no detail - 5MB rejection backend returns 400 with detail 'Archivo > 5MB' which DOES surface. Good. Just confirm formatApiError handles string detail correctly.
